title: Weil structures on operations and their basic maps
statement:
Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated finite-type morphism over the
finite base field, and let $f:X\to Y$ be its geometric fiber.
Use $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$ and the
Weil-complex categories.
On any of the stated domains on which the underlying operations
preserve bounded constructibility, pullback, the two direct images,
tensor and internal Hom carry canonical Weil structures. An
admissible
exceptional adjoint carries one as well. Tensor evaluation, the
adjunction units and counits, composition comparisons, exchange maps,
and the projection transformation are equivariant. The
coefficient twists carry their
prescribed Frobenius actions. These assertions concern the underlying
operations and their algebraic maps; equivariance of a geometric
smooth-purity orientation requires its separate theorem.
(For finite coefficients, a scheme-Frobenius form of the $Rf_!$
comparison, which also applies to non-invertible Frobenius coefficient
morphisms, is constructed later in [def-trf-weil-shriek-pushforward];
it is not used here.)

proof.text: Use the finite-field, coefficient and operation conventions of [def-fix-six-functor-datum] and the pair category of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Write $P_T=Lg_T^*$ for $T=X,Y$. The automorphisms of [def-weil-frobenius-detailed] satisfy $fg_X=g_Yf$, since $f$ descends to $k_0$. Their square is Cartesian: its horizontal arrows are isomorphisms, and its inverse is the square with $g_X^{-1},g_Y^{-1}$. These are semilinear scheme automorphisms, not generally $k$-morphisms. To apply [fix-lem-exchanges], equip the source corners with structural maps $s'_X=s_Xg_X$ and $s'_Y=s_Yg_Y$ to $\operatorname{Spec}k$, retaining the original structures on the target corners. Then $g_X,g_Y,f$ in that square are $k$-morphisms. The new corners are finite type over $k$: their structural maps differ by the field automorphism $\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$, an isomorphism. The horizontal arrows are separated and finite type because they are isomorphisms; the vertical arrows have these properties by hypothesis. The coefficient categories and operations depend on the underlying schemes and coefficient sheaves, so this change of structural map does not change them. Make the corresponding scalar twist whenever a semilinear automorphism square or its inverse is used below. By [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] and [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback], $P_T$ is exact inverse-image transport on integral representatives, with inverse transport along $g_T^{-1}$. The inverse-image equivalences induce inverse equivalences on complexes and their localizations. Their restrictions preserve the integral constructible categories by the latter lemma, and rationalization and the common-stage prescription in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] give inverse equivalences at $E$ and $\Qlb$. No assertion that scheme Frobenius is invertible is used.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 1–2: geometric automorphism square and coefficient interpretation

proof.text:
Here is the elementary lifting calculation used throughout. For a functor $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and a natural isomorphism $a:P_{\mathcal D}F\xrightarrow{\sim}FP_{\mathcal C}$, set $\theta_{FK}=F(\theta_K)a_K$. If $u\theta_K=\theta_LP_{\mathcal C}(u)$, naturality gives
$$\theta_{FL}P_{\mathcal D}(Fu)=F(\theta_L)F(P_{\mathcal C}u)a_K=F(u)F(\theta_K)a_K=F(u)\theta_{FK}.$$
Thus $F$ lifts on objects and morphisms to the fixed-pair categories of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]; it preserves identities and composition because $F$ does. If $v:F\to H$ obeys $a^H_KP_{\mathcal D}(v_K)=v_{P_{\mathcal C}K}a^F_K$, multiply by $H(\theta_K)$ and use naturality of $v$ to see that $v_K$ is equivariant. Composites, inverses of equivariant isomorphisms, and whiskerings of such maps satisfy the same equation by substitution. A single isomorphism is the datum in the pair definition; no additional continuity or independent iterate-cocycle hypothesis is required.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 1–3: formal fixed-pair lifting and equivariant maps

proof.text:
For $F=Rf_*$ or $Rf_!$, take $a^F=\operatorname{Ex}_*$ or $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ in the square of Step 1, as supplied by [fix-lem-exchanges]. The exchange is invertible without any general base-change-isomorphism assertion: horizontally paste the square with its inverse; the two exchanges, after whiskering with the inverse equivalences $P_X^{-1},P_Y^{-1}$, compose to the identity exchange by clauses (1)–(2). Pasting in the other order gives the other inverse identity. Hence
$$\theta_{Rf_*K}=Rf_*(\theta_K)\operatorname{Ex}_{*,K},\qquad
\theta_{Rf_!K}=Rf_!(\theta_K)\operatorname{Ex}_{!,K}$$
are isomorphisms and Step 2 gives the functors on Weil pairs. For $Rf_!$ at $E$ and $\Qlb$, use the actual higher-coefficient functors of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], rather than the finite-level-only definition: [fix-lem-exchanges] supplies their completed, rationalized and common-stage exchanges with all its specified domains, coefficient presentations and compatibility hypotheses retained. Its refinement compatibility identifies the structures for different compactifications. This does not claim preservation outside those domains.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 1–2: direct-image formulas, inverse squares, compact support

proof.text:
For $F=Lf^*$ take the comparison $a_L:P_XLf^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf^*P_YL$ obtained from $fg_X=g_Yf$ as $c_{f,g_Y}\circ c_{g_X,f}^{-1}$, where $c_{h,k}:L(kh)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*Lk^*$ are the pullback-composition comparisons. On finite module complexes these are [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. On integral constructible inputs, with completed pullback as in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and its product mapping-fiber model of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], they are the integral composition isomorphisms $c^{\mathcal O_E}_{h,k}$ of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition], whose reductions are the finite comparisons and which satisfy its associativity identity. Along the isomorphisms $g$ the completed pullback is the inverse-image transport by [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback]; the site equivalence of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] commutes with products, maps and differentials, which is how the transported models below are compared. Rationalize and pass to a common finite coefficient field as prescribed in that operation definition. Define $\theta_{Lf^*L}=Lf^*(\theta_L)a_L$. For tensor set
$$\theta_{K\otimes L}=(\theta_K\otimes\theta_L)\mu_{g;K,L}.$$
The comparison $\mu_g$ is the natural, composition-compatible isomorphism of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] at all the coefficient stages in use; thus Step 2, in two covariant variables, proves the tensor assertion. The same lemma gives equivariance of tensor associativity, symmetry and unit comparisons.

To obtain the internal-Hom comparison without a perfectness assumption, work first with modules over the completed integral coefficient sheaf and let $H$ be the inverse-image equivalence of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]. If $I$ is K-injective and $A$ is acyclic, every map $A\to HI$ corresponds under the inverse exact equivalence to a map $H^{-1}A\to I$, which is null-homotopic; applying $H$ to that homotopy proves that $HI$ is K-injective, directly by [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. The sheaf-Hom and product comparisons of [lem-pur-isomorphism-inverse-image-tensor-hom] and [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] give the chain isomorphism
$$H\mathcal Hom^\bullet(C,I)\cong\mathcal Hom^\bullet(HC,HI).$$
Its differential is preserved because $H(d_I\phi-(-1)^n\phi d_C)=H(d_I)H(\phi)-(-1)^nH(\phi)H(d_C)$. By the resolution definition [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and the identification of $Lg^*$ with $H$ in [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback], this gives a natural isomorphism
$$h_{K,L}:P R\mathcal Hom(K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom(PK,PL)$$
on every constructible pair where these values are in the prescribed category. Rationalization gives the comparison for arbitrary rational morphisms as well, by linearity in the two variables; the common-stage operation and scalar-extension comparisons of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] give it at $\Qlb$. Set
$$\theta_{R\mathcal Hom(K,L)}=R\mathcal Hom(\theta_K^{-1},\theta_L)h_{K,L}.$$
This is invertible, natural covariantly in $L$ and contravariantly in $K$. For a morphism of Weil pairs in the first variable use $P(u)\theta_K^{-1}=\theta_{K'}^{-1}u$, the rearranged Weil-morphism equation; this verifies the contravariant version of Step 2. Thus no assertion about site-perfectness or unrestricted Hom constructibility has been introduced.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 2–3: internal Hom under an equivalence, including evaluation

proof.text:
The internal-Hom comparison in Step 5 preserves evaluation: on complexes the map sends a local homogeneous homomorphism to its transported homomorphism, so, for homogeneous $x$ of degree $i$ and $\phi$ of degree $n$, evaluation in the order $C\otimes\mathcal Hom^\bullet(C,I)$ sends $x\otimes\phi$ to $(-1)^{in}\phi(x)$. Transport preserves degrees and the scalar $(-1)^{in}$, so both routes send this generator to $(-1)^{in}(H\phi)(Hx)$. This is exactly the compatibility with the tensor comparison of [lem-pur-isomorphism-inverse-image-tensor-hom]. The transport also preserves K-flat complexes: for a K-flat $C$ and an acyclic $A$, the tensor comparison identifies $HC\otimes A$ with $H(C\otimes H^{-1}A)$, which is acyclic because $H^{-1}$ and $H$ are exact; this is the test of [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Together with the K-injective calculation of Step 5, these transported resolution models induce the evaluation identity in the derived category, and we make the completed-tensor passage explicit. All schemes here are finite type over $k$, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. With $T=R\mathcal Hom(K,L)$ in the prescribed constructible domain, [lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion] gives the canonical isomorphism $\chi_{K,T}:K\otimes^L_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_E}T\xrightarrow{\sim}K\widehat\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}T$. The integral evaluation is the ordinary evaluation composed with $\chi_{K,T}^{-1}$. This comparison commutes with the exact transport $H$: on the flat-term K-flat representatives its quotient maps and transitions are the same maps after transport, while $H$ commutes with the products and differentials in the defining mapping fiber (Step 1). Thus the ordinary evaluation identity already proved remains an identity after conjugating by $\chi$. The completed tensor transport obtained this way is precisely [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], since both are obtained from the same finite quotient tensor comparisons before applying the product mapping fiber; the coefficient conventions of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] rationalize this same identity and represent it over a common finite stage. In particular, with $T=R\mathcal Hom(K,L)$, the equivariance square says
$$\operatorname{ev}_{K,L}(\theta_K\otimes\theta_T)\mu_{g;K,T}=\theta_LP(\operatorname{ev}_{K,L}).$$
Indeed precomposing a transported homomorphism by $\theta_K^{-1}$ and evaluating on $\theta_Kx$ cancels the two inverse maps. The identity is valid on the domains where the displayed evaluation and completed tensor are the supplied operations; it asserts no geometric purity identification.

Let $F=Rf_!$, $G=Rf^!$ be the specified admissible adjoint pair, with unit $
u$ and counit $\mu$. Use its adjunction and exchange normalization from [fix-prop-adjunctions], retaining the meaning of optional ambient admissibility in [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility]; nothing here asserts that every separated finite-type map satisfies ambient admissibility. Write $S=P_X$, $T=P_Y$ and $a:TF\xrightarrow{\sim}FS$ for Step 3. Take the mate
$$b:SG\xrightarrow{
u SG}GFSG\xrightarrow{G a^{-1}G}GT F G\xrightarrow{GT\mu}GT$$
of $a^{-1}:FS	o TF$, in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. By [lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences], $b$ is an isomorphism, since $S,T$ are equivalences by Step 1. Define $	heta_{GL}=G(	heta_L)b_L$ and apply Step 2. Expanding the mate formula and cancelling $G\mu\circ
u G$ and $\mu F\circ F
u$ by the triangle identities gives
$$(Ga)\circ(bF)\circ(S
u)=
u S,\qquad
(\mu T)\circ(Fb)\circ(aG)=T\mu.$$
Multiply the first equality by $GF(	heta_K)$ and the second by $	heta_L$, using naturality of $
u,\mu$: these are precisely equivariance of the unit $K	o GFK$ and counit $FGL	o L$. For $F=Lf^*$, $G=Rf_*$ use $S=P_Y,T=P_X$, and the pullback comparison of Step 4 as $a:TF	o FS$. Its mate is exactly the ordinary exchange comparison of [fix-prop-adjunctions] and [def-exchange-projection]. The same two equalities prove equivariance of the ordinary unit and counit. Thus invertibility of the exceptional comparison follows from equivalences, not from the generally false assertion that arbitrary mates preserve isomorphisms.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: exceptional adjoint and units/counits

proof.text:
For composable maps $Z\xrightarrow{u}X\xrightarrow{f}Y$ descending from $k_0$, write $a_f^P:P_Y P(f)\to P(f)P_X$ for either direct-image comparison of Step 3. Under the canonical composition maps, the vertical-pasting equation of [fix-lem-exchanges] reads
$$a_{fu}^P=(P(f)a_u^P)\circ(a_f^P P(u)).$$
Substituting $\theta_{P(f)K}=P(f)(\theta_K)a_f^P$ shows that $P(f)P(u)$ and $P(fu)$ have the same Weil map under their composition comparison. For pullbacks write $a_f^*:P_XLf^*\to Lf^*P_Y$. The corresponding equation is
$$a_{fu}^*=(Lu^*a_f^*)\circ(a_u^*Lf^*).$$
Expanding $a^*_{fu}$, $Lu^*a^*_f$ and $a^*_u\,Lf^*$ as in Step 4 into composition comparisons for factorizations of the single morphism $fug_Z=g_Yfu$, both sides become composites of comparisons $c^{\pm1}$ between the same iterated pullbacks; they are equal by the associativity identity of these comparisons (pseudofunctor coherence). At finite level the associativity is that of the termwise comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], which associate the same successive inverse images. At the integral stage it is the associativity identity of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition], an equality of integral morphisms, not one inferred from finite reductions; clause (1) of [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible] keeps all intermediate pullbacks in $D^b_c$. Rationalization and the common-stage prescription of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] retain the equation. Substitution of the Weil maps proves pullback-composition equivariance.
For a Cartesian square descended from $k_0$, denote its horizontal arrows by $h:Y'\to Y$ and $h':X'\to X$ and its vertical arrows by $f,f'$. Put $e: Lh^*P(f)\to P(f')Lh'^*$ for either exchange, without assuming $e$ invertible. Paste the square with the Frobenius squares in the two orders. Commutativity over $k_0$ identifies the outer rectangles. The horizontal-pasting and square-naturality equations of [fix-lem-exchanges] give, with canonical composition identifications inserted,
$$(P(f')a_{h'}^*)\circ(a_{f'}^P Lh'^*)\circ(P_{Y'}e)
=(eP_X)\circ(Lh^*a_f^P)\circ(a_h^*P(f)).$$
Multiplying by the images of $\theta_K$ and using naturality of $e$ is exactly the Weil-morphism equation for $e$. Give each source corner its scalar-twisted $k$-structure as in Step 1 whenever applying these equations. For the right-adjoint comparisons, [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], clauses (1), (2), and (4), takes the two equal pasted transformations, including identity squares, to equal mates. By the normalization of [fix-prop-adjunctions] these mates are the exceptional composition and exchange comparisons; Step 7 identifies their induced Weil maps, so they are equivariant as well. Equivalently each supplied mate is the unit–given-map–counit composite, so Steps 2 and 7 prove its equivariance directly. If its definition uses an inverse exchange, this applies on the specified domain where that exchange is invertible, and Step 2 gives equivariance of its inverse; no inverse of an arbitrary exchange is taken. These equations also cover diagrams supplied with commuting automorphisms in place of the descended Frobenius squares.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: composition and exchange equivariance

proof.text:
Expand the projection transformation using [def-exchange-projection]. Its ordinary direct-image factor is the transpose of
$$Lf^*(Rf_*K\otimes L)\xrightarrow{\mu_f}Lf^*Rf_*K\otimes Lf^*L\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_f\otimes1}K\otimes Lf^*L.$$
The tensor comparison is equivariant by the composition compatibility of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], and $\varepsilon_f$ and the unit used to transpose are equivariant by Step 7; hence their composite is equivariant by Step 2. For a compactification $f=pj$, the defining compact-support map is this projection for $p$, followed by $Rp_*$ of
$$j_!K\otimes Lp^*L\longrightarrow j_!(K\otimes Lj^*Lp^*L)\cong j_!(K\otimes Lf^*L).$$
For the open factor, form $\overline X'=\overline X\times_{Y,g_Y}Y$ with projection $\bar g:\overline X'\to\overline X$, an isomorphism because $g_Y$ is. The open base change $X\times_{Y,g_Y}Y$ is identified with $X$ by the pair $(g_X,f)$; this gives the transported open immersion $j':X\to\overline X'$. Thus the comparison uses an isomorphism between two compactifications and requires no Frobenius endomorphism of the chosen $\overline X$. The open projection map commutes with this transport: in the extension-by-zero presheaf of [def-weil-extension-by-zero] its map on tensor generators, for an object $V$ factoring through the open, sends $x\otimes y$ to the section $x\otimes j^{-1}y$ of the tensor sheaf on the open, and is the zero map otherwise; transport preserves the factorization condition, restriction of $y$, and this local tensor formula. These identical maps induce identical maps after sheafification and on the complex representatives used for derived tensor. At the integral stage use the compatible finite-reduction construction of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] and the supplied operation comparisons in [def-exchange-projection]. The sectionwise transport above is natural in the coefficient ring and commutes with every quotient map; hence it is an equality of the maps of reduction diagrams before applying $R\varprojlim$. Applying the product mapping-fiber construction of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] gives equality of integral maps. Rationalization and passage to a common finite stage preserve that equality. This uses the compatible diagrams, rather than inferring equality of integral morphisms only from equality of their separate finite reductions. Finally compare compactifications. By the refinement compatibility of [fix-lem-exchanges] (4), the Weil structure of Step 3 on $Rf_!$ is the exchange into $Rf_!^{c'}$ for the transported compactification $c'=(j',p')$ of $f$ (here $p'j'=f$ under the identification by $(g_X,f)$), followed by the refinement comparison $\rho_{c',c}:Rf_!^{c'}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_!^c$ and by $Rf_!(\theta)$. The calculation above identifies $P_Y(\operatorname{PF}^c)$, transported, with $\operatorname{PF}^{c'}$. By [lem-fix-projection-compactification-comparison], $\rho_{c',c}(K\otimes Lf^*L)\circ\operatorname{PF}^{c'}=\operatorname{PF}^{c}\circ(\rho_{c',c}(K)\otimes1)$. Composing these two equalities with the Weil maps of the inputs gives the Weil-morphism equation for $\operatorname{PF}^c$, for every choice of $c$. Thus the actual projection transformation is equivariant on its stated domain, without asserting its invertibility or using a purity orientation.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: projection as tensor and adjunction composites

proof.text: Use the canonical coefficient-twist Weil structures of [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists], not merely the underlying objects of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Their tensor powers and duals are exactly the constructions of Steps 4–6. By [lem-pur-twist-frobenius-scalar], geometric Frobenius on the Tate line over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is $q^{-1}$ and on the $m$-th twist is $q^{-m}$, including negative $m$ and $m=0$; these scalars commute with finite reduction and finite scalar extension. Pullback of the coefficient lines supplies the same prescribed structures on $X,Y$, by the roots-of-unity pullback construction in the twist definition. Tensoring the preceding equivariance identities with these lines gives the identities for twisted operations: the scalar factors multiply under tensor and invert under the contravariant argument, exactly as in Steps 4–6. This proves the twist clause. All constructions involved only algebraic operation maps; no conclusion about a geometric smooth-purity orientation has been made.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated finite-type morphism over the
finite base field, and let $f:X\to Y$ be its geometric fiber.
Use $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$ and the
Weil-complex categories.
On any of the stated domains on which the underlying operations
preserve bounded constructibility, pullback, the two direct images,
tensor and internal Hom carry canonical Weil structures. An
admissible
exceptional adjoint carries one as well. Tensor evaluation, the
adjunction units and counits, composition comparisons, exchange maps,
and the projection transformation are equivariant. The
coefficient twists carry their
prescribed Frobenius actions. These assertions concern the underlying
operations and their algebraic maps; equivariance of a geometric
smooth-purity orientation requires its separate theorem.

proof.text:
Write $g_X,g_Y$ for the geometric-Frobenius automorphisms of
[def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. For $Rf_*$, define its Weil isomorphism
by

$$
g_Y^*Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ex}_*}
Rf_*g_X^*K\xrightarrow{Rf_*\theta_K}Rf_*K.
$$

The exchange of [fix-lem-exchanges] is an isomorphism for an
automorphism square: the inverse comes from the inverse square and
their pasting is the identity. The pasting identity proves the
iterate compatibility required by
[def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. The same construction with
$\operatorname{Ex}_!$ defines the Weil structure on
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Pullback uses
$g_X^*f^*=f^*g_Y^*$. Tensor and internal Hom use the natural
identifications of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; for
internal Hom the inverse Weil map on its contravariant argument is
used. Since $g^*$ is an equivalence, this Hom identification does
not require a claim that every constructible complex is site-perfect.

For an admissible exceptional adjoint, take the mate of the
$Rf_!$ comparison under [fix-prop-adjunctions]. Inverse
automorphism squares again give its inverse, and mate calculus proves
that its units and counits are equivariant, using the adjoint of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility].
For the ordinary adjunction of [def-weil-derived-direct-image]
the same assertion is the definition of $\operatorname{Ex}_*$.
Evaluation is natural in the two Weil maps and their inverses, so
its square commutes. Composition and exchange use the pasting
identities of [fix-lem-exchanges]; the projection transformation
of [def-exchange-projection] is a composite of precisely these
tensor and counit maps, hence is equivariant as well.
Finally [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] fixes the scalar Frobenius
action on each twist, and tensoring with that scalar respects all
the maps above.
